turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: One hundred and forty-nine? Really! It seems to me that you possess a distressing lack of permanence, young man. I trust you are not suggesting that your future residence will be subject to the whims of a… Lady Bloxham?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Oh, no, Lady Bracknell, I assure you, I have absolutely no intention of residing subject to anyone's whims! My intentions are quite firm, and I hope to establish a… a settled home, you see. Belgrave Square is simply where my aunt happens to reside, and I visit her regularly.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: A settled home! How exceedingly vague! I must insist, young man, that you demonstrate a more concrete grasp of domesticity. Do you, at the very least, possess a landed estate?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: A landed estate? Well, I… I haven't precisely *inherited* one, Lady Bracknell, but I do have certain… responsibilities regarding a property in the country. It's a small place, you understand, but it's entirely mine, and I manage it myself!

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: “A property in the country, you say? Managed *yourself*? My dear boy, that sounds suspiciously like manual labour! I trust you do not spend your days grubbing in the soil like some… agricultural serf. One must maintain a certain distance from such vulgarities, you see.”,

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Really, Mama, you are being utterly ridiculous! Jack is perfectly acceptable, and besides, *I* am engaged to him, so your opinion is rather beside the point. A landed estate isn't everything, you know!

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, my dear, your youthful impetuosity is, as always, quite distressing. While I appreciate your… enthusiasm, a young lady's declaration does not automatically render a gentleman suitable! I must ascertain his character, you see, for the sake of propriety and, naturally, the future of my family.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Honestly, Mama, you're making a mountain out of a molehill! Jack is kind, he's attentive, and he adores *me* - those are far more important qualities than the size of his estate, wouldn't you agree?

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Kindness and attentiveness, you say? My dear Miss Fairfax, while those qualities are not entirely without merit, they are hardly sufficient to counterbalance a lamentable lack of fortune! I must inquire further, Mr. Worthing, about your family. Pray, tell me, are your parents, at least, respectable?

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mama, really! Must you interrogate the poor man as if he were a criminal? I’ve already told you, I adore him, and that should settle the matter entirely. It's quite embarrassing, you know, to witness such… scrutiny.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Embarrassment, my dear Gwendolen, is a small price to pay for safeguarding one's reputation! Mr. Worthing, I find your family history… remarkably vague. Pray enlighten me; I insist upon knowing precisely who one’s parents are, and what, if anything, they *do*.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: My… my parents, Lady Bracknell? Well, it’s a rather… peculiar story, actually. I was rather young when I was found in a handbag, you see, and I've never known them personally.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Found in a handbag, you say? Mr. Worthing, really! One has, of course, heard of abandoned infants, but to be discovered in a travelling bag is quite beyond anything I’ve ever encountered in my extensive experience of social proprieties. I find myself… intrigued, but also deeply, deeply concerned.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: A handbag, yes, Lady Bracknell. It was a rather large, plush handbag, left at Victoria Station. I was, naturally, quite small at the time, but the circumstances were… unusual, I admit. Perhaps I can elaborate further?

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: A handbag, you say? Victoria Station! My dear man, the very idea! One simply *cannot* proceed without ascertaining the provenance of this… receptacle. Pray, was it a Gladstone? A carpetbag? The details are, I assure you, of the utmost importance.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: A… a handbag, Lady Bracknell. I believe it was a rather fashionable one, though I wouldn’t presume to identify the maker. I was informed it belonged to a lady traveling to… somewhere, I’m afraid I can’t recall precisely where.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: A handbag, indeed! Mr. Worthing, I must confess, my sensibilities are quite overwhelmed. One's origins are, after all, a matter of the utmost importance, and a handbag is hardly a respectable foundation upon which to build a life, let alone a suitable match for my daughter.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I… I assure you, Lady Bracknell, it wasn't just any handbag! It was, as I understand it, quite the height of fashion at the time. Surely, even a fashionable handbag can be a beginning?

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: A fashionable handbag, you claim? My dear Mr. Worthing, you appear to believe that mere ornamentation can excuse a lamentable lack of pedigree! Pray tell me, does this handbag possess a family history? Has it been handed down through generations, perhaps with a crest or a notable stain?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: A family history? Good heavens, Lady Bracknell, I… I’m afraid I haven’t the slightest idea! I simply found it, you see, abandoned on a railway station. It seemed… well, it seemed rather forlorn.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: I am engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Pardon me, you are not engaged to any one. When you do become engaged to some one, I, or your father, should his health permit him, will inform you of the fact. An engagement should come on a young girl as a surprise, pleasant or unpleasant, as the case may be. It is hardly a matter that she could be allowed to arrange for herself . . . And now I have a few questions to put to you, Mr. Worthing. While I am making these inquiries, you, Gwendolen, will wait for me below in the carriage.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Mamma!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In the carriage, Gwendolen!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Gwendolen, the carriage!

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Yes, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: You can take a seat, Mr. Worthing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Thank you, Lady Bracknell, I prefer standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I feel bound to tell you that you are not down on my list of eligible young men, although I have the same list as the dear Duchess of Bolton has. We work together, in fact. However, I am quite ready to enter your name, should your answers be what a really affectionate mother requires. Do you smoke?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, yes, I must admit I smoke.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am glad to hear it. A man should always have an occupation of some kind. There are far too many idle men in London as it is. How old are you?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A very good age to be married at. I have always been of opinion that a man who desires to get married should know either everything or nothing. Which do you know?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I know nothing, Lady Bracknell.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am pleased to hear it. I do not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance. Ignorance is like a delicate exotic fruit; touch it and the bloom is gone. The whole theory of modern education is radically unsound. Fortunately in England, at any rate, education produces no effect whatsoever. If it did, it would prove a serious danger to the upper classes, and probably lead to acts of violence in Grosvenor Square. What is your income?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In land, or in investments?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: In investments, chiefly.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: What between the duties expected of one during one’s lifetime, and the duties exacted from one after one’s death, land has ceased to be either a profit or a pleasure. It gives one position, and prevents one from keeping it up. That’s all that can be said about land.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I have a country house with some land, of course, attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres, I believe; but I don’t depend on that for my real income. In fact, as far as I can make out, the poachers are the only people who make anything out of it.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A country house! How many bedrooms? Well, that point can be cleared up afterwards. You have a town house, I hope? A girl with a simple, unspoiled nature, like Gwendolen, could hardly be expected to reside in the country.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, I own a house in Belgrave Square, but it is let by the year to Lady Bloxham. Of course, I can get it back whenever I like, at six months’ notice.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bloxham? I don’t know her.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Oh, she goes about very little. She is a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Ah, nowadays that is no guarantee of respectability of character. What number in Belgrave Square?
